text:
dina: Heads-up — scheduling tenant_settings backfill (job tenant-settings-2026-03) tonight 23:00-00:30 UTC. 16 shards total.
dina: Goal is to keep window tight; planning 4 waves of 4 shards with a 60s spacing. Ops and SRE please watch.
eric: Sounds good. Can we set per-wave max-concurrency=1 and batch=800 to minimize lock hold?
frank: +1. Also add a safety gate: if replica_lag > 5s or lock_wait_avg > 100ms for more than 2 minutes, pause the waves.
db-sre: I can add alert rules on replica_lag > 5s (2m) and lock_wait_avg > 100ms (2m). Who triggers pause?
dina: We'll use deploybot holdpoints: I want a manual holdpoint after the canary wave. If trigger fires earlier, deploybot should auto-pause and ping #oncall-sre.
frank: CLI snippets: ```
# pin migration and set manual holdpoint
deploybot pin --migration=tenant-settings-2026-03 --version=20260315b --holdpoint=manual
# start after confirm
deploybot start --migration=tenant-settings-2026-03 --confirm
# pause/abort
deploybot pause --migration=tenant-settings-2026-03 --wave=3
```
eric: We'll also run a lightweight read cache warmup: cache_warmup=keys_prefix=tenant:settings: so first wave doesn't hit cold path.
db-sre: Added dashboards and alerts. I'll post snapshots to the thread if anything crosses thresholds.
dina: Timeline: pin at 22:50, canary wave (wave 1/4) 23:00, manual holdpoint 23:05 for ops signoff, then waves 2-4 23:10-00:10, final checks 00:10-00:30.
eric: Preflight checklist done: schema diff clean, sample backfill query <80ms on canary dataset. Linking runbook in the deploy doc.
frank: Note: we'll limit worker pool on the controller with `--workers=2` to avoid db connection storm.
deploybot: [bot] migration tenant-settings-2026-03 pinned by dina at 1740001118. Holdpoint=manual. Use `deploybot start` to begin.
dina: Pin confirmed. Ops please ACK when youre ready. :eyes:
db-sre: Acknowledged. Ill be on watch 22:45-00:45 UTC, will notify #oncall-sre on alerts. :white_check_mark:
eric: Starting canary wave now (1/4). Manual holdpoint will wait for SRE thumbs.
frank: Canary in progress — initial metrics: write p95 110ms, lock_wait_avg 45ms, replica_lag 0.7s.
db-sre: All green so far. Holding at manual gate for 5m.
dina: Manual signoff: holding OK, proceed to wave 2. :thumbsup:
eric: Wave 2/4 started. Lowering row_batch to 600 for this one as extra precaution.
db-sre: Alert — replica_lag spiked to 6.2s for 90s around wave 2. deploybot auto-paused at wave 2.
frank: Noted. Let's investigate. Any long-running queries on replica promotion or backup jobs?
db-sre: Found background analytics aggregate running overlapping our window. Kicked the analytics job, replica lag recovering.\erd: (typo)
eric: Good catch. Since deploybot paused, we will not advance to wave 3. We will resume wave 2 after lag < 2s for 3 consecutive minutes.
dina: No global rollback. This is a pause to stabilize. Please post exact resume command when ready.
db-sre: Replica lag back to 0.9s for 4 minutes. Recommend resume.
deploybot: [bot] resume request queued for migration tenant-settings-2026-03. Manual confirm required.
eric: Confirmed. Resuming wave 2. We'll keep workers=1 for next wave and increase wave_delay to 120s.
dina: Thanks. Also update release notes with the incident: note that analytics job overlaps can cause lag spikes; recommend scheduling analytics outside next backfill window.
frank: Wave 3/4 started with lower concurrency. Monitoring: write p95 150ms transient, lock_wait_avg 80ms, deadlocks 0.
db-sre: No further alerts. Replica lag steady.
eric: Wave 4 started. Final verification queries running.
dina: Final checks look good. Please add the short postmortem entry: cause=analytics overlap, mitigation=schedule change + lower worker default. I'll create a small follow-up ticket.
db-sre: Postmortem note added to release doc and ticket created: INF-3247.
frank: Runbook snippets saved and linked. :thumbsup:
eric: Closing threads and unpinning migration.
deploybot: [bot] migration tenant-settings-2026-03 unpinned by dina at 1740001125. Migration complete.
dina: Great work, thanks team! :tada:
